documentation.rationale: The identity half is solid: VIN, option-sticker photo, window sticker, Carfax snapshot with 12 service entries, and a clean-title claim. The maintenance half is missing: no invoices, no IMS proof, no scan data, and the seller confirms no records beyond the listing.

condition.rationale: Photos show glossy paint, a tidy interior with mild leather creasing, a clean trunk and a reasonably clean rear underside. The tires are under 6 years old. Against that, there is no PPI, the original single-row IMS is presumed, and there is no documented cooling, belt, coil or water-pump work at 22 years of age.

price_value.rationale: The likely hammer of $16k–$20.5k, informed by the prior $19,750 no-sale bid, sits at or below the low end of the $19,367–$26,295 fair-value band. An unaddressed IMS ($3k–$5k with clutch and RMS) and age-related catch-up offset part of that discount.

mission_fit.rationale: It is a manual with a strong point of view, likely within the ideal budget band, and an easy resale. It is not one of the named bridge candidates, and IMS risk on an undocumented single-row engine undercuts the 'reliable' requirement.

logistics.rationale: The car is in Pennsylvania, far from Carmel. The dealer allows inspection before close, but with about 12 hours left and weekday-only hours, a specialist PPI is hard to arrange. The sale is not inspection-contingent. Shipping is available. California smog status is unknown.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Carmon Red over Graphite Grey is an uncommon combination, and the car is a manual with low miles. It is a base 2.7, and the non-original wheels, fixed wing and side skirts dilute originality.

Up: the full Carfax shows regular dealer service, including coolant and plug work.
Down: over-revs in ranges 4–6, out-of-spec cam deviation, metal in the filter, or an oily IMS flange.
Down: the hammer runs past the fair-value midpoint with the IMS and age-related items still unaddressed.
Down: the decklid was drilled or the paint-meter readings show refinishing.
evidence.mission_note: A manual, low-mile 986 at a likely hammer inside the ideal band gives the bridge a clear point of view and easy resale. Its reliability case rests on an undocumented original single-row IMS, so it fits the mission only if a PPI before close clears the engine and the IMS retrofit is budgeted.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the VIN, the option sticker and the 2.7L decode all agree, a manual five-speed is confirmed, and the 29,233-mile odometer matches Carfax's last reading with three owners and 12 service entries. Maintenance evidence is thin. Only a 2025 oil change and A/C recharge are mentioned, and the seller confirms no further records. The seller also states the IMS bearing is original on an engine expected to carry the single-row design. Observed deviations from factory spec are the 18in wheels in place of the stickered 17in SportClassic, plus a fixed wing and side skirts that are not on the sticker, with the wing mounting method unanswered. Photos show good paint, a clean trunk, a reasonably clean interior and an underside with only light surface oxidation. All five model-critical items (IMS proof, DME scan, oil-filter evidence, borescope and an examined cold start) are missing or claim-only. One open recall is noted on Carfax and should be a no-cost dealer remedy. The no-reserve format and the prior $19,750 no-sale suggest a hammer near the low end of the fair-value band. The roughly 12-hour window leaves little time for an inspection before money moves.
evidence.next_action: Call a Lemon Squad or Porsche-specialist inspector near Douglassville, PA this morning to book a scan, cold-start and lift inspection before the 10:26 close. In parallel, ask the dealer for an engine-number photo and the full Carfax.
